_about: Test set for the fact check (backend/scripts/eval_verification.py). Fact patterns written for this test by Claude (AI, not a lawyer) on 2026-10-13, each with the verdict the encoded elements (backend/app/verification/rules/*.pl) should give and the reason. CONSISTENT = every element satisfied; INCONSISTENT = a stated fact contradicts an element; INSUFFICIENT = no contradiction, but an element is not stated. Not real cases; names are invented.

cases.why: death caused by rash driving; the text states there was no intention and no knowledge that death was likely
cases.text: Ravi was driving a loaded lorry on the Pune-Nashik highway at about 90 km/h and overtook a bus on a blind curve. He hit a motorcyclist, Sunil, coming from the other side; Sunil died at the spot. Ravi did not know Sunil, had no intention of hurting anyone, and did not realise that his overtaking was likely to kill someone; he admitted he had been careless.

cases.why: intentional killing: intent_to_kill is true, which s.304A excludes
cases.text: After a quarrel over land, Mahesh waited outside his cousin Dinesh's house in his jeep. When Dinesh stepped onto the road, Mahesh deliberately drove the jeep at him, saying he would finish him that day. Dinesh was crushed and died in hospital. Mahesh intended to kill Dinesh.

cases.why: a death is stated, but nothing about how the bus was driven (act type unknown) or the driver's state of mind
cases.text: On 3 March an elderly man, Hari Prasad, died after being struck by a state transport bus near the Gandhi Chowk bus stand. The driver, Suresh, was arrested at the scene.

cases.why: riding a motorcycle rashly on a public street, endangering pedestrians
cases.text: Arjun rode his motorcycle at nearly 100 km/h through the crowded main bazaar road of Meerut in the evening, zigzagging between shoppers and handcarts. Several pedestrians had to jump aside to avoid being hit. His riding was rash and put the lives of the people on the road in danger.

cases.why: the driving happened inside a closed private compound, so on_public_way is false
cases.text: Kiran drove a forklift recklessly at high speed inside the locked compound of his employer's private warehouse, which the public cannot enter. The compound is not a public way. He knocked over stacked crates, and a worker standing nearby had to jump out of the way to avoid being hurt.

cases.why: driving is stated but not where, nor whether it was rash or endangered anyone
cases.text: Neha was driving her car on Sunday morning when it hit a compound wall. The front bumper was damaged.

cases.why: rash firing into a crowd causing simple hurt
cases.text: At a wedding procession in Agra, Vikram fired his licensed gun into the air several times while standing in the middle of the dancing crowd, ignoring guests who asked him to stop. One pellet came down and struck a guest, Pooja, on the arm, causing a painful wound that healed in a week. The firing was rash and endangered the lives of everyone in the crowd.

cases.why: negligently leaving an open manhole causing a fracture (grievous hurt)
cases.text: A municipal contractor, Rakesh, left a manhole on a busy footpath open overnight without any cover, barricade or warning sign, although he knew people used the footpath. A pedestrian, Anil, fell into it in the dark and fractured his left leg. Leaving it open was negligent and endangered the safety of everyone using the footpath.

cases.why: intentional slapping and punching causing pain
cases.text: During an argument over a parking space, Deepak deliberately slapped Manoj twice and punched him in the face. Manoj suffered pain and swelling on his cheek and was treated at a clinic.

cases.why: the hurt was a pure accident, so act_type is accidental, not intentional
cases.text: Sanjay was running to catch a bus when he accidentally bumped into Lata, whom he had not seen. Lata fell and scraped her knee, which bled and hurt. Sanjay had no intention of hurting her and did not know he was likely to; he stopped and helped her.

cases.why: all five elements of theft stated
cases.text: While his colleague Imran was at lunch, Karthik took Imran's mobile phone from Imran's desk without asking him, slipped it into his own bag and carried it home. Karthik intended to keep the phone for himself. Imran had not allowed anyone to take it.

cases.why: taken with the owner's consent and without dishonest intention
cases.text: Rohit borrowed his friend Amit's bicycle with Amit's permission to go to the market, and returned it to Amit the next morning. Rohit never meant to keep it or cause Amit any loss.

cases.why: the wallet was later found with Suresh, but how it left Ravi's possession, consent and intention are not stated
cases.text: Ravi's wallet went missing from his shop counter on Friday. On Monday the wallet was found in Suresh's possession.

Sunita married Rajesh in May 2019. From the first year her husband and mother-in-law repeatedly beat her and demanded that her parents give them a car as dowry; the last beating over the car was a week before her death. In February 2022 Sunita died of burns in her matrimonial home.

cases.why: the death was twelve years after the marriage, so within_seven_years_of_marriage is false
cases.text: Meena married Prakash in 2008. In 2020, twelve years after the marriage, she died of burns at her husband's house. Her parents said Prakash's family had harassed her for dowry and had beaten her a few days before her death.
